title: Give Every Nation a Different Definition of Honor

voice.direction: A calm, fair-minded guide. Curious on the hook, plain on Mira's choice, warm admiration on 'courage', the same warmth for 'keeps everyone alive' so neither side sounds wrong. Weighing on 'Both are right about something', clear on the lesson, genuinely open on the question. No trailer voice.

lines.text: What if two honorable people could consider each other evil?
Mira walks away from the oath she swore at sixteen.
In the free towns, that's courage. No one should own your life.
In the valley league, it's betrayal. The levee she guarded keeps everyone alive.
Each side calls the other heartless. Both are right about something.
Give both sides real reasons, and let neither be entirely right.
Which matters more: personal freedom, or collective responsibility?

lesson: Give each people a moral system with a real reason behind it (freedom because no one should own a life; duty because everyone depends on everyone), put one person between them, and let neither side be entirely right.

youtube.title: Two Honorable People. Each Thinks the Other Is Evil. (Worldbuilding)
youtube.titleAlternate: How to write moral systems that clash
youtube.description:
What if two honorable people could consider each other evil?

Mira walks away from the oath she swore at sixteen: to keep watch on the levee that protects her valley.

In the free towns, that's courage. No one should own your life, not even a promise you made as a child. In the valley league, it's betrayal. The levee only holds because everyone holds it, so leaving puts everyone at risk. Each side calls the other heartless, and both are right about something.

That's how to write clashing moral systems: give each people a real reason for what it values (freedom, duty, loyalty, mercy), put one person between them, and let neither side be entirely right.

Which matters more: personal freedom or collective responsibility? Tell us in the comments.

Episode 14 of 50 in Worldcraft Shorts: Worldbuilding, from the ground up. Short lessons for fantasy writers, novelists, mapmakers and tabletop RPG creators.
